The current price for live cattle is around $116 and change per hundred weight. Since slaughter houses like cattle in the 800 lb range (their equipment such as hoists and overhead tracks limit the length of a carcass) that means that most small operators cull their herds in September. While the prices may rise after September the cost of feeding cattle also rises so the cost of the cattle is higher. So with 20 head going to market at I plan on making about 18K and change on my livestock this year.I will also have about 300 tons of premium alfalfa pellets for market. Current market prices is about $190 per ton. I generally get between 4 to 5 tons per acre with three cuttings. I have a pelletizer so I don't rake and bail. I use a PTO driven mower that just cuts the alfalfa and lets it lay in the field. When the alfalfa is dry i use a side mounted rake with a pick up to blow dump the alfalfa into a trailer. From the field the alfalfa goes to the pellitizer and then into bags. I like this method as it is less labor and time consuming and I get a whole lot less lossage. With the pelletizer I can add other ingredients to customize the pellets for each feeders needs. After the pellets are bagged, the bagged pellets are a lot easier as the bags are loaded on pallets which are moved and loaded by fork lift. With palletized bags the transporter doesn't need a flat bed trailer as the bags of pellets can be loaded into standard tractor trailer rigs. I should get about $60,000 for my alfalfa this year. Now you have to understand that there is a lot of cost to raising livestock and alfalfa but farm prices have been going up recently with the exit of the California producers out of the market because of water issues.
